Cute platformer that evokes visual styles of the PS1/N64 era while putting on refined 3D platforming techniques. Amazing music combined with several unique and interconnected areas provide for a solid game. The abilities you get feel very intuitive and make for a fun experience. I hope we can get more.
one minute you are lost for hours calling it the worst game ever but then you find the key and it is a masterpiece. also the movement is so good

I'm usually not great at metroidvanias but this game is genuinely so good. Like it starts off pretty fun and then evolves to have some of the most satisfying movement I've ever experienced since I played Bomb Rush Cyberfunk. I genuinely have no clue what the intended route for most of this game even is but like, it was really fun just trying to whatever until i figured it out and the actual movement mechanics make this game so satisfying. Like I have no clue how to get to the second switch in the Underbelly Major Key room but I got there without using it and it was so cool.

Extremely fun, but at times also really confusing Platformer/Metroidvania

The only complaint i got, is that i didn't knew where find the keys and having to rely to a guide for the last two, after spending 4h+ on traversing the map to find nothing major.

Otherwise this game is one of the best platformers i've played.

Before I beat the game: (no spoilers at all)
Fun and simple, but a waste of time. It lacked any sort of depth albeit this is their first game ie no map upon release (later fixed)[Major oversight]. I enjoyed the majority of the game. When it came to end game it felt much more tedious to backtrack looking for ominous clues and wandering around hoping you had all the power-ups because you made it this far without looking anything up right? Well it's staying that way because the online community will give you the vaguest answer possible as if there's a boom stick tied to their lips. Gods rest the boogeyman keeping these people's lips tied shut, still going to beat the game but god does the lack of information feel insufferable. 4/5 keys and I'm barking into a padded cell wondering how to snake through a section.

After I beat it:
Literally 30 minutes-1 hour later after the initial review. I beat the game and I feel empty man. Gained all these power-ups, got the keys, and beat the boss for some rinky dink dialogue that reveals the goat lady's name. Fantastic. I hope their next game has some elevated thought to it. Maybe I'm spoiled by games like Neon White and Outer Wilds, but I need there to be genuine levels to the structure of the levels and more than 5 enemies if their function is low level.

Explore the world of Pseudoregalia, collect movement abilities in order to overcome platforming challenges you can't yet clear. Or Not. Fuck it. Perform a slide into a super somersault then 3 perfect wall kicks in a row and a backflip.

The progression is so loose it's almost an open world, as long as you Believe (and also want a bit more challenge, as the game is relatively easy without sequence breaking )

Fairly simple game, that understands what makes a metroidvania special. Very odd wall jump mechanic though.

Overall I enjoyed it, the movement (the primary game mechanic) is enjoyable and gets moreso as you gather your powerups. The frustrations I had were mostly my own fault for being a big dummy and not paying attention. There's NO guidance/handholding so it's entirely on you to make note of your surroundings so that you know what areas are now accessible when you get a new ability. The ending was extremely abrupt and there isn't really much of a story if that matters to you.

Actual time to beat: 10-12 hours, but a LOT of that was me wandering in circles

The story, decorations and concept are simple yet they are so enchanting. The music is on another level, the whole setting is just beatiful. Overall, majestic experience, I'd love to see more of Sybil's jorneys.
Genuinely so good. Yes it's kind of short, but it's 1000% worth it's price. Can't wait to see what's next!

The movement feels incredible. It's so much fun moving around the game world. The music is great & the N64 style presentation is spot on. Both of these elements mix together really well to create a unique yet familiar atmosphere that I can't get enough of.

Unfortunately the combat & final boss felt extremely out of place & I think the game would have benefited if they weren't in the game at all. When I dropped into that final boss arena instead of a final platforming gauntlet my heart sank & it left a sour taste in my mouth. I also think a (very simple) map would have made navigating the world a bit more bearable as I found it a bit too confusing at times.

Still absolutely worth playing, especially if you like the retro aesthetic & 3D platformers.
If hitting that slide jump -> sideflip -> wall kick -> pole cancel backflip to get the ledge combo doesn't make you nut, the goat ass will.

Fantastic 3d platformer with a very fun moveset to play with. The game was short but it felt just right before overstaying it's welcome. The music and overall nostalgic vibes of the game are a huge plus, would love to see more from this developer in the future!

This game is an absolute banger! 

I highly recommend anyone who likes 3D platforming, metroidvanias, movement games, or just fun games in general give it a go.
Very good and fun, was easy for me but for some could be hard or take a while to beat. would recommend

Absolutely amazing game with a really sweet and small story punctuated by some of the best movement tech I've had the joy of playing with in a platformer. Sections that "require" specific abilities can be overcome without them if you figure out a specific trick or combination of moves. The entire game is arranged in a way where you can explore from any direction towards any direction.

It's just hugely satisfying. Finally pulling off a time trial or clearing a messed up jump you weren't sure was possible comes packed with that sweet, sweet dopamine.

No spoilers here but what little story is in here is super enjoyable. Totally worth it overall, grab yourself a copy.

An insanely fun open-world platformer for just 5 bucks.

Go on, buy it. Thank me later.

Easily one of the best platformers I've ever played. Oozes with style and the movement feels super fluid. The combat feels a liiiiiittle clunky but that isn't the focus of the game so whatever. One thing that would be an amazing feature that'd take this game to an 11/10 is either a community workshop to publish your own maps or an in-game map maker, but as it stands very solid game that is absolutely worth the price.

I saw some gameplay online and knew I had to check this out. Pseudoregalia delivers perfectly on gameplay, level design and visuals. It captures N64-style graphics better than any "retro" style game you see flooding Steam and Itch.io with their crappy PS1-esque visuals.

The movement of your character is the star of the show here, as you progress through Pseudoregalia's small but dense world, you'll find yourself upgrading your ability to traverse the environment and find lots of bonus unlockables along the way. It's incredibly satisfying to explore, learn and improve on your maneuverability as you discover your objective and reach new areas in the game. 

TLDR: The gameplay is smooth and excellent, the visuals are simple but pleasing and the game overall is a real treat for anyone interested in platformers or Metroidvania style games. If you have the pocket change to spare, this game is an easy sell. 

10/10, I wish it was longer.

At times, Pseudoregalia almost gave me an aneurysm, as it felt like I was playing some weird metroidvania version of Getting Over It. At times it's charm gripped me and didn't let me go until I finished the game. And at times, it was so gøddamn hard for my smol brain that my fingies kept forgetting which buttons they should press next.

Nevertheless, this game is absolutely gorgeous. The N64 feeling alone would be enough to give Pseudoregalia a thumbs up since it evokes so much nostalgia for me, but there's also so much love put into it. That and when you get the jist of how the movement gimmicks work, it's so fun and impressive.

Completed it now, so now I can form a better opinion on the game!

While the game is more movement and platforming focused, it's a nice change of pace compared to combat heavy games, that and the obstacles to obtain Aspects, Health or new powers are decently balanced in challenges.

It's also pretty neat how some challenges can be done without certain power ups, but instead with creative use of your abilities.

The Soundtrack I'm also quite pleased with. They fit the stages they are placed in fairly well. Like the Underbelly's soundtrack fits the aesthetic of the dark caves and underground structures, and the Library having a calming track.

Also the different clothing options are pretty neat. Though I am partial to the Sol Sister skin.

lastly, there are some pretty cool level mods that can be added in to better hone your movement and abilies, like Shmoovement School or other QOL mods, like an Attire UI that shows you what the skin looks like before accepting it. There are also a few funny attire mods like Plushy Sybil one can download.

I'd recommend this game as it's very good for the price, and worth sinking a few hourd into!

But still, why does the Goat Cat Bunny Lady not have trousers?

The combat could use some work and the environments are a bit on the blocky side, but otherwise it's a really fun romp throughout this game's world. Movement is great and extremely smooth & the level design lends itself to it perfectly.

Has literal breadcrumbs of story, the combat is pretty barebones, and the game itself is relatively short, but that aside, the movement system (it's main selling point) is very amazing. It really gives you a lot of freedom on what you can do, specially when you unlock all the movement power ups. If you think whatever you're about to do is possible, highly likely the game will let you do it. Except if that's grabbing Sybil's ass, though.

Soundtrack? Very good, specially the underbelly track, which is a personal favorite. It slaps harder than I would slap Sybil's ass.

Overall, I do recommend it because I did end up liking it. It does have a slow and infuriating start, but again, once you get the movement power ups, it really, REALLY makes up for it. If you're stuck though, you can think while staring at Sybil's ass. It helps.

I have mixed feelings on this one.
Goat-Bunny lady = 11/10
Controls and Mechanics = 9/10
Music and sound = 7/10
However!!
Platforming 6/10
Level Design 4/10

This game is freaking CONVOLUTED, with pathways and hidden entrances everywhere. It is extremely overwhelming with paths splitting up, often leading to entirely new zones you're not supposed to go until much later, but the game gives you no hint, and you can easily waste 20 minutes in the new zone, before you encounter the big obstacle that requires a new power, forcing you to backtrack. It's always a 50/50 of whether you're supposed to "progress" or backtrack.
And this happened several times during my playthrough.

The game is absolutely a labor of love and passion, however it NEEDS a map of some kind, as it is a literal maze most of the time.

An absolute delight to play, the platforming feels really tight, and relatively unique in it's implementation.
Honestly would've loved a significantly longer game, but at the price point it feels really fair whats on offer here.
Game can at time feel quite meandering, but I think that's by design, really goes hard on the old school metroidvania gameplay, You can go wherever you want, and I hope you remember why you couldn't progress past this area otherwise you're going to be wandering around trying to remember.
Personally not a problem for me as a fan of the genre, but something to be aware of for anyone that's considering it.
I loved this game and highly recommend it :)

Absolutely stellar music, movement, area design, combat, character design, etc.
This game is extremely polished and addicting, absolutely recommend.

Controls are really frustrating and never clicked for me. And there's a lot of platforming in this game so the bad controls start to get really annoying. There's also a weird problem where you can go to certain areas of the game early before you have the proper upgrades and when you get there you're soft locked and have to load a previous game. I get this game is going for an old N64 vibe but even N64 games had more polish than this.
Absolutely phenomenal 3D platformer with satisfying and elegant movement. The visual style feels nostalgic and comforting. Plus goat-bunny-cat lady.

I can only describe this game as "If Mario 64 had Metroidvania elements". The game had many highs, and some lows. By the end I was a little frustrated about the lack of fast travel, but I get it. It wouldn't fit the vibe to have that in here. It's got that classic retro feel, and I think the lack of some QoL features such as fast travel or map markers really adds to that. The problem is, I suck at platforming and movement. So the game was pretty difficult and by the end, I was spending way too much time just failing or trying to figure where tf I should be going.

Because of those reasons, I couldn't say I absolutely loved the game. I was expecting a more action focused game so my expectations are partially to blame. However, if you've been looking for a Metriodvania that's more focused on the movement and platforming than the combat, this games for you.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (97%): most reviews praise the gameplay and combat, which is the game's main draw.
The most common complaint is also the combat, though only a minority of reviews raise it.

details.text: Reviewers who had played only briefly are less positive at 81%, while longer-playing reviewers are nearly unanimous.
Recent reviews are still 94% positive, with fewer people now complaining about combat and slightly more about the story.
